answer:
**Ejecutado. Resultado principal: 38/97 = 39.2 % de los estudios replicados en Psicología van liderados por un profesor júnior en la línea de la replicación (`seniority.r`), IC de Wilson 95 % 30.1 %–49.1 %.**

## Hipótesis final (frase única, autocontenida)

> Assuming a seniority hierarchy that the dataset itself does not define (Professor > Associate Professor > Assistant Professor > Assistant > Researcher) and counting "junior professor" as Assistant Professor or Assistant — i.e. the assistant level, with Researcher excluded as non-professorial — roughly two in five of the replicated studies in Psychology were led by a junior professor: among all 97 original–replication pairs of the Psychology replication project (`project == "rpp"`, all with usable seniority) 38 have a junior most-senior author on the replication line (`seniority.r`), i.e. **38/97 = 39.2 % (Wilson 95 % CI 30.1 %–49.1 %)** — a share that rises to **16/35 = 45.7 % (CI 30.5 %–61.8 %)** if one restricts to the studies that *additionally* replicated successfully (`replicated == 1`) — whereas on the original-study line (`seniority.o`) not a single one of the 97 has an assistant-level lead (0/97 = 0 %; only 5/97 = 5.2 % if Researcher is also counted as junior), because the replicated originals were overwhelmingly full professors (83/97), so the "junior professor" share is a property of the replication teams, not of the original papers.

## Composición dentro de rpp (n = 97) y cruce solicitado

| categoría | `seniority.r` (principal) | `seniority.o` (paralelo) |
|---|---|---|
| Professor | 19 | 83 |
| Associate Professor | 24 | 9 |
| **Assistant Professor** | **23** | 0 |
| **Assistant** | **15** | 0 |
| Researcher (no profesoral) | 16 | 5 |

Difieren en **77/97** filas; cruce `seniority.o` (filas) × `seniority.r` (columnas): Professor→{Prof 16, Assoc 21, AsstProf 21, Assistant 13, Researcher 12}; Associate Prof→{1, 2, 2, 2, 2}; Researcher→{2, 1, 0, 0, 2}. De las 38 filas junior en `seniority.r`, 34 tienen original liderado por un catedrático → la junioría no se hereda del paper original.

## Cuadrícula de sensibilidad (todas las celdas con k/N y %)

`seniority.r` (PRINCIPAL)
| definición | F0 todos rpp | F1 drop==False | F2 replicated==1 | F3 drop==False & replicated==1 | F4 dedupe título |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 AsstProf | 23/97 = 23.7 % | 22/90 = 24.4 % | 10/35 = 28.6 % | 10/31 = 32.3 % | 23/95 = 24.2 % |
| **D2 AsstProf + Assistant** | **38/97 = 39.2 %** | 36/90 = 40.0 % | 16/35 = 45.7 % | 16/31 = 51.6 % | 38/95 = 40.0 % |
| D3 + Researcher | 54/97 = 55.7 % | 50/90 = 55.6 % | 20/35 = 57.1 % | 18/31 = 58.1 % | 53/95 = 55.8 % |

`seniority.o` (paralelo)
| definición | F0 | F1 | F2 | F3 | F4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | 0/97 = 0.0 % | 0/90 = 0.0 % | 0/35 = 0.0 % | 0/31 = 0.0 % | 0/95 = 0.0 % |
| D2 | 0/97 = 0.0 % | 0/90 = 0.0 % | 0/35 = 0.0 % | 0/31 = 0.0 % | 0/95 = 0.0 % |
| D3 | 5/97 = 5.2 % | 5/90 = 5.6 % | 1/35 = 2.9 % | 1/31 = 3.2 % | 4/95 = 4.2 % |

IC de Wilson por celda (ej.): D2·F0 30.1–49.1 %; D2·F1 30.5–50.3 %; D2·F2 30.5–61.8 %; D2·F3 34.8–68.0 %; D2·F4 30.7–50.1 %; D1·F0 16.4–33.1 %; D3·F0 45.8–65.2 %; D3·F0 (`seniority.o`) 2.2–11.5 %.

## Verificaciones (petición 1)

Los conteos de F2 sobre 35 filas son enteros y coherentes con los porcentajes: D1 10/35 = 28.6 %, **D2 16/35 = 45.7 %**, D3 20/35 = 57.1 % (tu lectura de 16 y 20 confirmada). Además: 97 ids únicos, 0 duplicados de fila; las categorías de seniority son exactamente las 5 documentadas y suman N en ambas líneas; D1 ⊆ D2 ⊆ D3 (23 ≤ 38 ≤ 54); `replicated` no tiene ausentes en rpp (35/62); 7 filas `drop == True` conservadas en el principal y retiradas en F1 (n = 90); 2 títulos duplicados con ids distintos conservados en el principal y deduplicados en F4 (n = 95, donde D3/`seniority.o` pasa de 5 a 4 porque el par rpp.148/149 es Researcher).

**Contexto descriptivo (no es la pregunta):** éxito de replicación 16/38 = 42.1 % con lider júnior vs 19/59 = 32.2 % con lider sénior; Fisher exacto bilateral p = 0.388 → no significativo, no se afirma relación.

## Limitaciones

1. La etiqueta documentada de `seniority.r` es copia literal de `seniority.o`; tratarla como "autor más sénior de la replicación" es **inferencia empírica** (77/97 filas difieren; `seniority.o` en rpp no tiene ningún nivel assistant), no hecho documentado.
2. "Junior" es una suposición mía sobre la jerarquía, no un campo del dataset; si Researcher se cuenta como júnior la cifra sube a 54/97 = 55.7 %, si sólo cuenta Assistant Professor baja a 23/97 = 23.7 %.
3. El dataset codifica **sólo el autor más sénior por estudio**, así que la proporción es por estudio-liderazgo, no por autor individual.
4. File B (`..._replication_success_data...`, 143×15) no tiene campo de seniority: se usó sólo como confirmación de que "Psychology" = `project == "rpp"` (71/73 coincidencias por apellido, mediana |po − p_value.o| = 2.5e-4) y nunca en numerador ni denominador.
5. La exclusión de roll-ups `aggregated == True` (26 filas de ml1/ml3) se aplica globalmente para no duplicar estudios, pero es un no-op para rpp (todos NaN).

payload.workflow: 1) Loaded File A (meta-regression_study_data_...csv, 927x57) and File B (meta-regression_replication_success_data_...csv, 143x15). 2) Excluded study-level roll-ups (aggregated == True; 26 rows, ml1/ml3 only) to avoid double counting -> 901 rows. 3) Primary population: project == 'rpp' (Psychology project) = 97 rows, 97 unique ids, one row per O/R pair; seniority.o and seniority.r 0% missing, so N = 97. 4) Numerator: seniority.r in {Assistant Professor, Assistant} (junior definition D2, tier order assumed) = 38 -> 38/97 = 39.2%, Wilson 95% CI 30.1-49.1%. 5) Parallel column seniority.o (D1/D2 = 0/97; D3 with Researcher = 5/97) plus seniority.o x seniority.r crosstab (77/97 rows differ) and per-category distributions. 6) Sensitivity grid 5 filters (F0 all rpp 97; F1 drop==False 90; F2 replicated==1 35; F3 both 31; F4 dedupe repeated titles 95) x 3 junior definitions (D1 AsstProf; D2 +Assistant; D3 +Researcher) x 2 seniority lines, every cell reported as k/N and % with Wilson CIs. 7) Integrity checks: unique ids, no row duplicates, category counts sum to N, D1 subset D2 subset D3, integral F2 counts (10/35, 16/35, 20/35). 8) Confirmatory (not used for numbers): surname-heuristic join of File B project=='Psychology' rows onto rpp (71/73 matched, median |po - p_value.o| = 2.5e-4) to verify that 'Psychology' == project 'rpp'; File B has no seniority field. 9) Descriptive contrast: replication success 16/38 = 42.1% junior-led vs 19/59 = 32.2% senior-led, Fisher exact p = 0.388 (not significant).
